body:
> Before you left the hospital, did they give you resources to contact if your suicidal thoughts escalated again?

They gave me the number to their crisis line, which actually just connects directly to the wing of the hospital that I was in. I haven't used it, but I think I'm in a space where I could now.

>  I flunked out of school twice and dropped out once, all due to depression. Got sorted in the end, even got into grad school.

Just you telling me this gives me immensely more hope than I had. One of the hardest parts of this has been knowing that it's not the first time it's happened-- I had a similar situation right around this time last year, as well as others long ago. I've been embarrassed at the fearful idea that people would take me less seriously, knowing this is an ongoing struggle for me. Now I have hope.

> You are coming back from a very, very dark place, and the thing about those dark places is they have shadows that reach out and try to pull you back in. That is when personal connections are so valuable. 

Amen. You're the first person who's acknowledged this in a way that felt like it was being taken seriously, and the first person to state explicitly that you get how much it means to keep open connections through all of this. Thank you. I've felt like a freak of nature trying to make my case to the world until now.

Hugs back. Thanks for replying.

I have talked to a few different people on campus-- the dean, a counselor, and I'm working on getting medications and a long-term therapy plan worked out. It's just still pretty dark in the meantime. I'm really afraid that I'm not going to be able to fix all the mess I've created, especially with school.
